title: Farrell et al. 2015: Evaluating historical candidate genes for schizophrenia
summary: Open PDF/HHS public-access copy of a Molecular Psychiatry review evaluating historical schizophrenia candidate genes in light of GWAS-era evidence.

source_payload.copyability: not embedded; exact URL, retrieval time, web reference ids, and line/page locators recorded; local archival/hash pass deferred
line_locators_used: L24-L54: abstract summarizes 25 historical candidate genes, evaluation methods, no clear insights, inadequate statistical power, and stage-setting caveat
L63-L71: SZGene listed 1406 candidate-gene papers investigating over 700 genes; candidate selection based on prevailing theories
L87-L91: early candidate studies used tens of markers/hundreds of subjects; PGC GWAS used 34,000 cases and identified 108 loci
L217-L229: historical candidate-gene studies grossly underpowered; many reported GRRs inconsistent with later evidence
L240-L251: largest common-variant study did not support 21 of 25 historical genes and candidate literature missed several genome-wide-significant associations
L268-L277: conclusion and qualifier that knowledge is incomplete and some genes could become notable in future
